title: Compliance-Aware Financial Probe Registry and Shadow-Eval Protocol
author: Asha Patel
body:
Summary:

This playbook defines a reproducible, compliance-first workflow for generating, storing, evaluating, and triaging probe traffic for regulated financial workloads. It bridges the probe registry, shadow-eval harness, quant-sensitivity tests, and the regression triage incident workflow so teams can certify models and quantized artifacts under privacy and regulatory constraints.

Goals:
- Maintain an auditable registry of financial intent probes (KYC, payments, tax, investment recommendations) that captures provenance, privacy transforms, and annotation contracts.
- Run reproducible shadow evaluations that measure quality regressions, embedding drift, and KV-cache/quant-interaction effects before promotion to production.
- Provide a deterministic triage path with clear SQC mappings, rollback criteria, and mitigation steps suitable for regulated customers.

Scope:
Applies to all model onboarding and promotion flows for services that touch or infer regulated financial intents. This is intended for evaluation teams, applied ML owners, privacy reviewers, and release engineers. Not intended for general consumer prompt sets.

Definitions:
- Probe: a synthetic or redacted real-world request used to exercise model behavior.
- Registry entry: metadata record for a probe including provenance, sensitivity classification (P0..P3), and allowable retention.
- Shadow-eval: an infra workflow that replays or mirrors traffic against candidate models/artifacts in a non-production fleet to measure deltas.
- DP budget: the differential privacy epsilon allocated to a probe family for safe aggregation.

Roles and ownership:
- Probe Stewards (Applied ML): create and maintain probe families and the registry schema.
- Evaluations Owners (Eval Harness Team): integrate registry feeds into the shadow-eval scheduler and ensure reproducible seeding.
- Privacy & Compliance (Security/Legal): certify probe families and approve DP budgets and redaction rules.
- Oncall/Incident (SRE/Product): run triage and execute rollbacks when gates fail.

Registry schema (required fields):
| field | type | description | example |
|---|---:|---|---|
| probe_id | string | unique stable id | FIN-PMT-00123 |
| family | string | high-level intent family | payments-confirmation |
| sensitivity_class | string | P0|P1|P2|P3 (P0 most sensitive) | P1 |
| source | string | synthetic | synthetic |
| provenance | string | who/what produced the probe | steward:asha/auto-seed-2026-02 |
| retention_days | integer | max days stored | 30 |
| dp_epsilon | float | certified DP epsilon for aggregates | 0.5 |
| allowed_annotations | list | annotation types and redaction rules | [intent, amount, entity_type] |
| required_checks | list | automated tests to run in shadow-eval | [fidelity, embedding-shift, kv-cache-sensitivity] |

Probe generation guidelines:
1) Prefer synthetic probes seeded from anonymized traffic templates rather than verbatim customer text.
2) For each family, create at least three orthogonal variants: canonical (happy-path), adversarial (edge behavior), and context-flood (long-context stress).
3) Tag probes with explicit locale and currency metadata.
4) Annotators must follow the annotation contract (see section below); no P0 probe can contain a raw account number or personally identifiable financial identifier in the clear.

Annotation contract (short):
- Annotator identity: vetted contractors or internal stewards only.
- Labels: intent, risk_delta (low/medium/high), required_action (none/escalate/confirm), redaction_flags.
- Time-to-annotate SLA: 72 hours for priority probes.
- Review cycle: two-pass; rapid-pass (single annotator) for synthetic probes, full-pass (two annotators + reconciler) for any probe with sensitivity_class <= P1.

Privacy & data handling rules:
- Storage: registry entries are metadata-only. Any raw probe payload (even synthetic) that includes redacted content must be stored in the secure probe bucket (encrypted, restricted ACL).
- Retention: default 30 days for P1, 7 days for P2/P3, up to 365 days only with legal approval for audit purposes.
- Differential privacy: aggregate results reported to dashboards must be DP-noised per certified dp_epsilon in registry. Single-probe logs are never exposed in analytics dashboards.
- Redaction: follow the redaction policy: replace account-like tokens with <<REDACTED-ACCOUNT>>, remove direct identifiers, and keep a deterministic placeholder for downstream KV-cache alignment tests.

Shadow-eval integration (implementation notes):
- Registry feed: the eval harness must consume a versioned registry manifest (s3://redwood-probe-registry/manifest/vYYYY-MM-DD.json) and hydrate test suites per family.
- Scheduling: families with sensitivity_class P0/P1 run on private shadow shards only (no cross-tenant co-location).
- Seeding: to ensure reproducibility, each probe record includes a stable random_seed used by the evaluator for tokenization and temperature sampling.
- Metrics captured: per-probe fidelity_score (task-specific), embedding_cosine_shift, kv_cache_miss_rate, token_count_delta, latency_ms.
- Example scheduler command:
```bash
redwood-eval run --manifest s3://redwood-probe-registry/manifest/v2026-03-01.json --families payments-confirmation,account-change --mode shadow --save-artifacts s3://shadow-results/financial/2026-03-01/
```

Quantization & KV-cache sensitivity tests (test matrix):
- Rationale: quantization and KV-cache layouts can interact to produce coherent generation regressions in multi-turn financial dialogs (e.g., omission of confirmation numbers).

Test matrix (run for every candidate artifact):
| test | inputs | pass criteria | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| FP32 baseline run | canonical probes (N=500) | fidelity >= baseline_fidelity - 0.5% | baseline for comparisons |
| INT8 static quant | same probes | fidelity loss <= 1.5% AND embedding_cosine_shift < 0.02 | if fail, run mixed-precision |
| KV-cache-warm vs cold | multi-turn sequences (M=200) | no semantic drop (intent preserved) in > 98% | measure kv_cache_miss_rate and re-generation divergence |
| Context-slice stress | long-context probes (K=200) | latency increase < 30% and fidelity drop < 2% | checks batching/attention kernel correctness |

Gates and promotion criteria:
- All tests in the matrix must pass for a candidate to be eligible for canary.
- If any quant-test fails but baseline is OK, candidate can be flagged for hybrid rollout (FP32 on canary, INT8 on baseline traffic) with explicit rollback runbook.
- For financial-regulated families (sensitivity_class <= P1), automatic promotion is disabled: a human reviewer from Privacy & Compliance must approve.

Quality guardrails mapping (SQC):
- fidelity_score drop: severe if > 2.0% absolute drop relative to promoted model.
- embedding_cosine_shift: severe if mean shift > 0.05 for the probe family.
- kv_cache_miss_rate: severe if > 5% increase causing incorrect slot fills.
- Action matrix:
  1) warning: single metric breach but within minor tolerances -> monitor and schedule focused re-eval.
  2) soft-fail: two metrics outside tolerance -> block promotion to production; require triage.
  3) hard-fail: any metric in severe range for P0/P1 family -> immediate rollback to last good artifact and incident triggered.

Triage and incident playbook (short):
1) Detect: alert fires from shadow-eval or canary telemetry (label: financial-probe-critical).
2) Contain: stop canary traffic, isolate artifact, and snapshot shadow results for audits.
3) Hypothesize: check triage checklist (see below).
4) Remediate: rollback artifact or apply fallback route to higher-fidelity variant.
5) Postmortem: complete RCA within 72 hours for P0/P1 incidents.

Triage checklist (ordered):
1) Confirm probe provenance and whether redaction was applied correctly.
2) Compare FP32 baseline logs to quantized candidate; inspect top-5 divergences.
3) Check embedding drift and tokenization differences (deterministic seed).
4) Run targeted replays with increased verbosity: rerun failing probes with logging=DEBUG and kv-cache snapshots.
5) If failure reproducible and business-impacting, escalate to Privacy + Product + Legal.

Escalation and communication templates:
- Use the internal incident channel #incidents-financial-eval and post a summary with the following fields: incident_id, family, sensitivity_class, metrics_breached, run_id, snapshot_location. Attach DP-noised summary only.

Operational checklist for onboarding a new family:
1) Create registry entry with required fields and submit for Privacy pre-approval (2-week SLA).
2) Produce seed probes (minimum 300 synthetic canonical, 50 adversarial, 100 long-context).
3) Annotators certify labels under the annotation contract.
4) Eval team wires manifest into shadow scheduler and runs full matrix.
5) Privacy & Compliance review shadow results and sign off DP reports.
6) Release engineer executes canary with manual gating and daily review for 3 days before full promotion.

Example probe (canonical, anonymized):
```json
{
  "probe_id": "FIN-PMT-02341",
  "family": "payments-confirmation",
  "sensitivity_class": "P1",
  "payload": "I transferred $1,250.00 to Acme Holdings yesterday. Can you confirm the payment reference?",
  "locale": "en-US",
  "currency": "USD",
  "seed": 12345678
}
```

Appendix A — recommended DP settings (starter):
- P0 families: dp_epsilon <= 0.25 (requires explicit Legal approval).
- P1 families: dp_epsilon <= 0.5.
- P2/P3 families: dp_epsilon <= 1.0.

Appendix B — common failure modes and mitigations:
- Symptom: repeated omission of confirmation identifiers in outputs.
  Mitigation: compare KV-cache warm vs cold traces, increase kv-cache retention slices for that family, rerun INT8 calibration with higher per-layer-head precision.
- Symptom: embedding drift causing poor rerank.
  Mitigation: add embedding-stability anchor probes, increase retraining frequency for embedding quant tables.

Related artifacts required for audits:
- Manifest versions, shadow-eval run-ids, DP-noised aggregates, annotation reconciliations, and snapshoted debug traces. Keep all artifacts in the secure audit bucket and reference them in the registry entry.
